explanation: The pole fires on the contentless 'seam' token at which one unit of text ends and the next begins: in prose the token that plants the onset of a new predicate (infinitival ' to' and, more weakly, modals 'will/can/may/could' and clause-level 'and'/'or' before a bare verb; 'please' and clause-initial adverbs such as 'simply'/'effectively' before an imperative verb; the comma that closes a fronted adjunct; an opening quote; a sentence-final '.'), and in code the layout tokens that open a new line or statement (line-leading whitespace runs, ';', '{', '=', brackets). The same tokens inside a unit do not fire - prepositional ' to' ('drove to the house') and list commas score about 0, as do the head words on either side of the seam (the verb itself, determiners, prepositions, pronouns, identifiers) - with the response graded by how stereotyped the seam's left context is ('In a bowl,' fires strongly, 'In a pot,' barely).
